title: Somebody Left The Porch Light
subject: coming home after a long absence
caption: Gospel soul. Hammond organ through a rotating speaker, upright piano, bass, live kit, tambourine on two and four, hand claps. A powerful female lead sings with heavy melisma and full-chest belting; a choir answers every line in call and response and stacks harmonies under the final chorus, which modulates up a semitone. Recorded live in a room with natural bleed and long gospel-room reverb. 92 BPM, E-flat major. Rising, communal, grateful.
lyrics:
[Intro - Organ]

[Verse 1]
Seven years is a long walk back
I counted every mile in my chest
The mailbox leans the way it always leaned
And somebody left the porch light on

[Pre-Chorus]
(Still burning) still burning
(Still waiting) still waiting

[Chorus]
Somebody left the porch light on
After everything I said
I don't deserve that yellow square of glass
But Lord, I'm walking to it anyway

[Verse 2]
My mother's hands are smaller now
She don't ask me where I've been
She just puts another plate down
Like I never left the room

[Bridge - Choir]
(Come on home) come on home
(Come on home) I'm coming

[Chorus - key change]
Somebody left the porch light on
After everything I said
I don't deserve that yellow square of glass
But Lord, I'm walking to it anyway

[Outro]
Still burning
Still burning
